business_problem: water-link needed to centralize and operationalize real-time telemetry from hundreds of thousands of digital water meters so billing, maintenance, leak detection and stakeholder integrations could run automatically instead of through disconnected manual processes.
solution_summary: water-link and partner delaware built a central data hub on Microsoft Azure with Databricks at the core so smart-water-meter telemetry could drive operational action instead of sitting in disconnected systems. Job clusters connect to Azure Event Hubs to ingest streams from more than 200,000 digital meters, then enrich those messages with asset and customer data before routing signals to operational teams and downstream platforms. Databricks SQL warehouses and Delta Lake make the curated data broadly consumable across service-desk, field-service and analytics teams, while Power BI provides a 360-degree cockpit and Azure Functions bridges Databricks outputs into the SAP integration stack so ERP workflows can be triggered directly from reports. An OpenAPI-based layer supports internal and future external sharing, and the rule engine prioritizes hundreds of thousands of daily alerts so leak, theft and contamination responses can be automated without human triage.

data_flow: Digital-meter telemetry streams into Azure Event Hubs and is processed by Databricks job clusters, where the data is enriched with asset and customer context and stored in Delta Lake. Databricks SQL and Power BI serve insights to business teams, while Azure Functions passes selected outputs into SAP and other operational systems for automated action.
business_outcome: water-link now supports more than 20 use cases with a single data hub, processes hundreds of thousands of alerts without human triage, enables direct ERP actions from reports and gives consumers and operators faster insight into leaks, contamination risks and service events while lowering operational loss.
